entries.title: TianshanOS API User Guide
entries.text: Connect your own scripts and systems to monitor the device, control its computers, receive live status, run remote tasks, and maintain configuration and updates. This guide assumes familiarity with HTTP, JSON, and basic server operations; circuit and firmware knowledge is not required. This guide is based on TianshanOS 0.6.4.

entries.title: Find your task
entries.text: Task Start here Make your first API call Quick start Identify the controller and the two computers Devices and names Monitor temperatures, fans, power, and computers Monitoring Switch power or the USB connection Device control Start and verify a remote service Remote tasks Configure variables, sources, actions, and rules Automation and Configuration models Transfer files or update firmware Maintenance and Transfers Receive live status and results WebSocket Look up an API Complete reference Investigate errors or maintain a long-running integration Troubleshooting and Operations

entries.title: Reading order
entries.text: Complete a read-only request in the quick start first. Then follow the scenario for your task, including its result checks and recovery steps. Open the reference when you need individual parameters. The documented default accounts admin / root and initial password rm01 are product defaults. Other addresses, filenames, tokens, and response values are illustrative. Use the actual address and current password of a device you manage. Examples contain no private tokens, changed passwords, or real application records. The reference covers 277 registered names in 28 functional groups, including config.pack.apply, which is retained but does not apply generic configuration. Dedicated file / image routes and WebSocket messages have separate chapters. A registered name does not guarantee that the required hardware, storage, credentials, or remote service is ready.

entries.title: Quick start
entries.text: Connect, log in, and read a protected measurement. Apart from creating and closing a login session, this sequence only reads status.

entries.title: Set the device address
entries.text: Use the device's current IP address. WebUI and business APIs use HTTP port 80 by default, so no explicit port is normally needed. The API prefix is /api/v1. Replace the example address with your own device address: export TSBASE='http://10.10.99.97' For connection problems, check the IP address, network, and service state. See Troubleshooting.

entries.title: Read controller information
entries.text: curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/system/info" Illustrative response excerpt: {"code":0,"data":{"app":{"name":"TianShanOS","version":"0.6.4","compiledate":"Nov 5 2026","compiletime":"10:00:00"},"chip":{"model":"ESP32-S3","cores":2},"uptimems":123456}} Check HTTP status and then code. Version is at data.app.version; uptimems is milliseconds. Do not assume a top-level data.version field.

entries.title: Log in and retain the session
entries.text: The default accounts are admin and root, both with initial password rm01. Log in and use the APIs permitted for that account. If you have changed the password, use your current password. Set umask 077 before creating login.json and restrict access to the file. This example uses the default admin account: {"username":"admin","password":"rm01"} umask 077 curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @login.json \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/auth/login" > login-response.json export TSTOKEN="$(python3 -c 'import json; r=json.load(open("login-response.json")); assert r["code"] == 0; print(r["data"]["token"])')" Successful data contains token, sessionid, username, level, expiresin in seconds, and passwordchanged. Use token as the credential; sessionid is only an identifier. Use the returned token for subsequent calls. Access follows data.level and endpoint authorization. Password changes are an optional account-management operation through auth.changepassword. Handle password files, login responses, and tokens as credentials. Remove temporary credential files after use.

entries.title: Read a protected temperature
entries.text: curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/temp/read" Illustrative excerpt: {"code":0,"data":{"temperaturec":42.5,"temperature01c":425,"source":"variable","timestampms":120000,"valid":true}} temperaturec is Celsius; temperature01c is tenths of a degree. Only use the reading as valid when valid:true. Missing or invalid data must not become 0 degrees in your monitoring system.

entries.title: Log out
entries.text: curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \ -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/auth/logout" unset TSTOKEN POST logout returns {"success":true}, rather than the usual code / data envelope. Scripts and connections using the session need a valid session again. Next, choose a task scenario or use the read-only Python example supplied with the editable documentation.

entries.title: Devices and names
entries.text: TianshanOS manages both its controller and the connected computers. Identify the target before calling an API: their status values describe different things. User-facing name API identifier Purpose Management controller system. TianshanOS version, memory, tasks, and controller restart Inference computer device:"agx" Power state, power control, and reset; monitor. provides compute telemetry Application computer device:"lpmu" Power state, power control, reset, and upper-level network access setup Cooling fans fan. and numeric id RPM, control mode, temperature curve, and output limits Touch light, board light, matrix display touch, board, matrix Colors, effects, images, QR codes, and text Local storage /sdcard/... and other supported paths Files, configuration packages, and supported update materials Remote host Saved SSH host id / host Server commands or managed processes; not necessarily one of the built-in computers Use agx and lpmu exactly as the API identifiers. For example, the application computer is still addressed as {"device":"lpmu"}.

entries.title: Interpret measurements correctly
entries.text: Fan duty is the output percentage, from 0 to 100. RPM is rotational speed. Unknown duty may be null; also check dutyvalid. Temperature source may be a local sensor, compute telemetry, a variable, or a manual test value. Check the source, valid flag, and timestamp. powergood is a hardware power indication. It does not establish that the operating system or application is ready. USB target selects a shared USB route. Switching it can interrupt traffic on the previous route. runid identifies a managed remote service run. A retained record does not establish that its process is still running; verify its status. Operation receipt contains an operation identifier and result credentials. Preserve the complete receipt rather than just a display name.

entries.title: Three stages of completion
entries.text: The API accepts the request, for example by returning started:true. The device action or remote process reaches the requested state. Your application becomes ready, for example by passing a health check. Confirm the stage your task requires. Restarting the controller, powering a computer, and starting its application are separate operations.

entries.title: Task scenarios
entries.text: Examples use TSBASE and TSTOKEN from the quick start. Replace addresses, object IDs, configuration versions, and receipts with actual values. Control examples have real effects: use only the task you intend to perform.

entries.title: Monitor the device
entries.text: Read temperatures, cooling, power, and computer status into your monitoring system. Log in for READ capabilities; some overview endpoints are public. curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" "$TSBASE/api/v1/temp/read" curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" "$TSBASE/api/v1/fan/status" curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" "$TSBASE/api/v1/power/status" curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" "$TSBASE/api/v1/device/status?device=agx" Retain temperature valid, fan dutyvalid, power valid / crcvalid, and last update times. Display invalid or disconnected states explicitly. duty is a percentage; rpm is rotational speed. Computer state=on does not establish application readiness. See Response models. Successful monitoring means valid readings that keep updating. Use WebSocket for a continuous dashboard. For invalid temperatures, inspect temp.sources; for compute telemetry problems, inspect monitor.status. Do not replace missing values with zero. The supplied Python example performs login, reads, and logout only.

entries.title: Control a computer
entries.text: ADMIN is required. First read device.status to identify agx or lpmu and its current state. Use an explicit on / off action rather than repeating toggle after a timeout. curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary '{"device":"agx","action":"on"}' \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/device/power" Then GET device.status and inspect state / powergood. Confirm application readiness on the target computer or through a business health endpoint. For normal shutdown use off. forceoff / reset interrupt work and can lose data; arrange target-system maintenance first. To switch USB, POST device.usb.set with {"target":"agx"}, then GET device.usb.status. Other targets are esp32 / lpmu / disconnect. The old route may disconnect during the switch; that alone is not a device fault. After a timeout, query state before retrying. Preserve error state, power indication, and details if the target does not reach the expected state.

entries.title: Adjust lights and fans
entries.text: Routine LED operations need ADMIN. GET led.list to obtain a device name, then fill it: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary '{"device":"board","color":"#00A0FF"}' \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/led/fill" Read led.list again. To use the display after restart, separately POST led.save with {"device":"board"} and inspect saved. Displaying and saving startup settings are different steps. For fans, read fan.status / config first. POST fan.set with {"id":0,"duty":50} only after obtaining the actual fan ID. fan.mode selects off / manual / auto / curve. Curve, limits, and persistence permissions are listed in the Fan reference. Check dutyvalid / duty / targetduty, temperature, and faults after changing output. Restore the intended control mode after a temporary manual setting.

entries.title: Manage remote tasks
entries.text: Use ssh.exec / execstream for a one-off command; use a saved SSH command and run record for a continuously managed service. Raw command execution requires ROOT; starting an existing managed service requires at least ADMIN. Before starting, confirm reachability, a verified host fingerprint, and a saved host referencing a valid SSH key. Unknown / changed fingerprints are verified through ssh.test and trusted information, not by clearing trust or automatically accepting. With root, read ssh.hosts and ssh.commands. Check host, command, servicemode, and readiness matching. See Configuration models. Read the latest activeversion and start the saved service: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary '{"commandid":"YOURSERVICECOMMANDID","activeversion":"CURRENTVERSION"}' \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/ssh/services/start" Retain runid and operationid. POST automation.services.status with {"runid":"YOURRUNID","verify":true}. Inspect operationphase, busy, and state. verify connects to the original host; it is not just a local cache read. Verify application health / readiness. To stop, POST automation.services.stop with the original runid and continue querying status. A runid is not a ready indication; lastknown is a previous observation. Deleting configuration or a local key does not stop remote processes. Use the original run identity rather than guessing a process by name. For a one-off stream, authenticate WebSocket before POST ssh.execstream. Keep the complete receipt and use ssh.execstatus after interruption. Never rerun a command merely to retrieve missing output. See Streaming SSH for execution, matching, and output completeness.

entries.title: Configure automation
entries.text: The flow is: acquire data, map it into variables, then execute an action when conditions hold. With root, read automation.status / config.status first. Resolve loading, enablement, pause, or SD-source selection issues before editing. Start with a saved user variable: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/automation/config/status" Use its activeversion in the next request: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-binary '{"name":"example.temperature","value":42.5,"activeversion":"CURRENTVERSION"}' \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/automation/variables/set" Read automation.variables.get with root to confirm value, readonly, and sourceid. Retain the new activeversion. Create an enabled:false rule from the rule model; use a log action before adding power or remote-execution effects. Add a real data source only when needed. Verify data arrival, variable updates, and stale status before enabling the rule. Saving a definition, enabling configuration, starting the engine, and executing actions are separate states; saved:true alone is insufficient. Refresh and merge after a conflict. Preview deletion impact. Preview / apply SD or backup selection. Respect pause / busy results rather than overwriting managed files.

entries.title: Maintain the device
entries.text: Choose one maintenance goal at a time so its effects can be checked. Goal Sequence Completion Back up an object Export with the role required by that object; save tscfg; preview any later import Complete package retained and verifiable; export is not recovery Save a file Upload, inspect attributes, download and compare Intended path, length, and bytes Update firmware / WWW Check matching images, transfer, read global progress, confirm state, restart if needed Correct running identity / version and working application Change networking Record old access / configuration, change, save, reconnect Management and target networking both work Change a password changepassword, log in again, update client sessions New credentials work; old sessions are no longer assumed valid Install identity certificate Check CSR / key match, install, inspect cert.status and client trust Correct material, actual loaded identity, and verified client connection See Transfers and updates for complete requests and capacity limits. cert. manages device identity, key. manages SSH keys, and hosts. manages remote fingerprints. After failure, establish which stages took effect before retrying or recovering.

entries.title: Paths and methods
entries.text: Business URLs have the form http://10.10.99.97/api/v1/.... Dots in a logical name become path separators: fan.status maps to /api/v1/fan/status. Preserve case, including key.exportPrivate and log.setLevel. Use only the methods listed for each API. Read operations usually allow GET / POST; writes usually allow POST / PUT / DELETE, with some POST-only endpoints. This guide generally uses GET for simple queries and POST for actions. A disallowed method returns HTTP405. Names and parameters determine the action. Do not infer that DELETE always deletes an object or POST always creates one.

entries.title: Sessions and roles
entries.text: Protected requests carry Authorization: Bearer <token>. Do not place tokens in URLs. A role or sessionid supplied in ordinary request JSON does not establish that identity. Access label Meaning Public This capability can be accessed without login; resource conditions still apply READ At least read permission; authorized admin / root sessions normally qualify ADMIN Routine device operations; admin or root required ROOT Raw command execution, automation definition writes, and selected account management; root required Body token Authentication APIs validate the token JSON field; this is not anonymous permission to change accounts Default accounts are admin / root, both with initial password rm01. The policy distinguishes READ / WRITE / ADMIN / ROOT, but this does not imply an API for creating arbitrary accounts at all levels. No registered endpoint has minimum WRITE in this version. Some resources or parameters add checks: ordinary file reads may allow READ; sensitive paths require ADMIN. config.get exposes only the language preference publicly; other keys require ADMIN. Full SSH host / command, rule, and action reads normally require ADMIN; secrets in automation.sources.list still require ROOT. temp.bind queries allow ADMIN, while binding changes require ROOT. automation.proxy.fetch inherits destination permissions for local APIs and requires ROOT for external services. restricted:true means fields were filtered; never save omitted fields back as empty values.

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Use Content-Type: application / json and a JSON object body. Arrays belong inside object fields. Avoid duplicate keys and overlapping query / body parameter names; conflicts are rejected. Query values are decoded once and may be interpreted as integers or booleans. Prefer JSON for objects, arrays, floating-point values, null, and identifiers whose leading zeroes must be preserved. Do not URL-encode twice. Optional means that omission is permitted; null is not generally equivalent to omission. Some binding APIs explicitly use null to clear a binding. Time units are field-specific: milliseconds, seconds, or Unix time.

entries.title: Determine the result
entries.text: Usual success: {"code":0,"data":{"example":"value"}} Business errors can still use HTTP200: {"code":1,"error":"invalidrequest"} Explanations may be in error or message. data may be an object, an array, or absent. A successful response need not contain message. Handle non-success HTTP status as a transport, authorization, format, or service failure. If code is present and nonzero, handle a business error. Check the endpoint's valid, success, exitcode, persisted, or operation status. A top-level success does not replace these checks. For asynchronous work, use the completion flow specified by that API; retain a receipt when one is returned. After a disconnect or resultunknown, inspect state before retrying. Login, logout, binary uploads, and downloads have dedicated formats. A successful download body contains file bytes, not JSON.

entries.title: Error codes
entries.text: code Name Suggested response 0 OK Check the endpoint's completion conditions 1 INVALIDARG Check fields, types, ranges, and version conditions 2 NOTFOUND Refresh object / operation information; do not invent or reuse stale IDs 3 NOPERMISSION Check role, sensitive resources, and export conditions 4 BUSY Inspect active work and wait before retrying 5 TIMEOUT Determine whether a result exists before repeating a write 6 NOMEM Reduce request size or load; preserve known results 7 INTERNAL Retain the reason; investigate state if resultunknown 8 NOTSUPPORTED Use a supported entry point 9 HARDWARE Inspect the device, sensor, and configuration 10 CONNECTION Check network, remote host, fingerprint, and service 11 AUTH Reauthenticate or complete the required verification SSH trust flows also use1001/1002 for unknown / changed host fingerprints and provide fingerprint details. Verify through a trusted channel before confirming; deleting trust records is not identity verification.

entries.title: Effects and persistence
entries.text: applied reports an applied setting; persisted or saved reports storage success. They can differ. An error may occur after an earlier stage has taken effect: retain its details and read back state. Toggles, rule triggers, remote execution, and updates are not guaranteed safe to repeat. Read-only queries may be retried with appropriate load control. After a write timeout, query state or the receipt first.

entries.title: Limits
entries.text: Connections, bodies, receive times, and task slots are bounded. Identity and size checks can reject a request before consuming its entire body. Avoid replacing live subscriptions with large numbers of concurrent polls. This version allows up to 1 MiB for the generic JSON route with a30-second receive budget; authentication requests are limited to 16 KiB/10 seconds. Configuration packages themselves are limited to 64 KiB. Individual APIs can impose smaller limits. See Transfers for binary routes. JSON nesting is limited to 32. Embedded NUL, trailing garbage, and duplicate keys are rejected. For HTTP413, reduce the request or use the feature's designated upload route.

entries.title: Common response models
entries.text: These fields are inside data. Handle HTTP status and code as described in Common rules. Fields vary with device state, initialization, and role. Preserve unknown when a field is missing; do not fill it with 0 or false.

entries.title: temperature
entries.text: Field Interpretation temperaturec Celsius. Both fields represent the same measurement. temperature01c Tenths of a degree Celsius. The same measurement as temperaturec. valid Whether the value is usable; false must not be treated as normal temperature source Source of this reading; interpretation depends on the API. activesource Actual source; interpretation depends on the API. preferredsource Preferred source; interpretation depends on the API. timestampms, lastupdatems Milliseconds since device start, not Unix time stale, agems Staleness / age in milliseconds; null may mean never updated partialstale, validcount, stalecount Partial failure of a multi-variable binding; inspect more than its average The implementation bounds valid temperature values. Inputs can come from local sensors, compute telemetry, variables, or manual tests. A manual value does not establish the physical temperature.

entries.title: fan
entries.text: fan.status returns a different shape depending on whether you supply id: With id: one fan. Without id: fans, plus temperature, tempvalid, and tempsource. Field Type, unit, or meaning id Fan number. mode Control mode: off, manual, auto, or curve. dutyvalid Whether the output is valid. duty Known actual duty, in percent. Unknown duty is null. targetduty Target output percentage; can differ from actual duty rpm Revolutions per minute; interpret with tachometer capability and faults enabled Whether the fan is enabled. running Whether the fan is running. Unknown running state can be null. fault Fault state. temperature Relevant control temperature, in Celsius controltemperature Control temperature, in Celsius. guardtemperature Protection temperature, in Celsius. predictedtemperature Predicted temperature, in Celsius. slopecpermin Temperature slope in Celsius per minute autostate Automatic-control stage. guardactive Whether protection is active. tempstale Whether temperature data is stale. controllergain, coolingresponse Diagnostic values, not RPM or temperatures applied and persisted distinguish application from storage. Requesting 50% does not establish a valid physical 50% output.

entries.title: power
entries.text: power.status combines voltage, chip measurements, protection, and statistics. Use the specific voltage / chip/protection.status APIs for details. Field Unit or meaning voltagev Voltage, in V. currenta Current, in A. powerw Power, in W. voltagemv mV; convert before comparing to V valid Data validity. Check both fields for chip measurements. crcvalid Communication integrity. Check both fields for chip measurements. timestampms Milliseconds since start state Protection stage. countdownremainingsec Remaining countdown, in seconds. initialized Whether initialization is complete. running Whether protection is running. device.power.status reports measurements for individual power rails instead: Field Meaning voltagemv Rail voltage, in mV. currentma Rail current, in mA. powermw Rail power, in mW. totalpowermw Total power, in mW. Compute telemetry can also use mW. Follow each field's unit.

entries.title: config-result
entries.text: Configuration writes and source selection return a set of state flags; not every response contains all of them. Field Meaning activeversion Current configuration version; use the new returned value for the next write source Active configuration source loaded Loaded state. Separate from the other state flags. configured Configured state. Separate from the other state flags. enabled Enabled state. Separate from the other state flags. paused Paused state. Separate from the other state flags. saved Storage completed. uncertain Outcome uncertain. loaderror Active-configuration error. internalerror Internal-backup error. sdavailable Whether SD is available. internalexists Whether an internal backup exists. internalvalid Whether the internal backup is valid. comparisonknown Whether comparison is possible. backupmatches Whether the backup matches. Unknown is not a match. awaitingsdchoice An SD selection is required internalsavedat Internal backup save-time information collection Collection location. id Object location. dependency Dependency location. impact References and runs affected by deletion / replacement Preview packagedigest and credentialgeneration are apply preconditions, not reusable global authorization. restartrequired:false does not replace loaded/enabled or runtime checks.

entries.title: variable
entries.text: Variables include name and type/valuetype. The following fields may also be present: Field Meaning value Variable value. sourceid Source identifier. persistent Persistence information. readonly Whether the variable is read-only. flags Variable flags. lastchangems, lastupdatems Change and update time fields. agems, stale Age and staleness information. For variables.list, use includevalue to request values and includemeta to request metadata. A missing value field is different from a null value.

entries.title: certificate
entries.text: cert.status reports the following separately: Field Meaning hasprivatekey Whether a private key is present. hascertificate Whether a certificate is present. hascachain Whether a CA chain is present. Certificate information Information about the certificate. HTTPS diagnostic-service status Status of the separate diagnostic service. Certificate validity may depend on timeready. An undetermined result must not be treated as valid. An installed identity, the identity loaded by the separate HTTPS diagnostic service, and diagnostic-client trust are separate checks. Inspect service status after installation. Business APIs remain on HTTP; their Bearer roles are separate from mTLS certificate roles.

entries.title: color
entries.text: RGB components range from 0 to 255. Direct color APIs accept: A supported color string. An object with r, g, and b. A decimal integer equivalent to 0xRRGGBB. JSON does not allow hexadecimal numeric literals. led.color.hsv uses different ranges: Field Meaning h 0–359 degrees. s, v 0–255, not percentages. Color correction is an object with the following structure: Field Meaning enabled Overall enablement. whitepoint Nested enabled, redscale, greenscale, and bluescale. Scales range from 0 to 2. gamma Nested enabled and gamma. The gamma range is 0.1–4. brightness, saturation Each contains nested enabled and factor. Send the corresponding nested objects when modifying them. Device brightness (0–255) and a correction factor use different units.

entries.title: ota
entries.text: After starting an update from a URL or SD, read ota.progress. It reports device-wide state; there is no private receipt for each login. Field Meaning APP progress state, percent, totalsize, receivedsize, message. WWW progress state, percent, total, received, message, running. APP: pendingreboot means a restart is needed. WWW: completion is indicated by state=completed and running=false. 100 percent alone does not prove the new version is running. Partition information includes: Field Meaning label, address, size Partition label, address, and size. Bootability Whether the partition is bootable. version, project Version and project information, when available. canrollback Whether rollback is currently available. aborted acknowledges the cancellation call. Continue checking progress and actual state. Binary uploads use a separate response. The following combination means that Flash was written but the SD recovery cache was not fully saved: HTTP 409. status=partial. error=recoverycachefailed. flashwritten=true. Inspect partitions and recovery files before retrying.

entries.title: network
entries.text: Ethernet reports interface and configuration state separately: Field Meaning interfacepresent Whether the interface exists. linkup Physical link state. configerror, configerrorname Configuration-application errors. A connected cable does not establish that IP configuration succeeded. Distinguish actual state, requested state, and the stage at which an error occurred: Field Meaning DHCP running Actual state. Ethernet wantrunning Requested state. restoreerror Configuration-restoration error. applyerror Configuration-application error. resumeerror Service-resumption error. 0 means that the corresponding step reported no error. Check the interface and link state before deciding whether the service should run.

entries.title: Configuration models
entries.text: These models save hosts, commands, sources, actions, and rules that the device can use at runtime. Save a disabled example and read it back before enabling effects.

entries.title: Read the version before writing
entries.text: With root, read automation.config.status and retain activeversion. Put it at the top level of a write. After each successful write, use the new version for the next request. For rule updates, also carry the read revision as expectedrevision. A conflict requires rereading and merging, not merely replacing the version token and replaying stale input. The JSON objects below are complete request-shape examples. Replace CURRENTVERSION, identifiers, addresses, keys, and variable names. Place model fields at the request top level; do not add a config wrapper except for explicitly shown subobjects. restricted:true can indicate a metadata-only view. Use ADMIN for complete SSH host / command, rule, and action reads; automation.sources.list secrets still require ROOT. Writing definitions follows each endpoint's required role. Omitted secret fields are not empty values. Host / source updates merge with existing JSON; command / action updates should carry complete definitions. Rules use their own merge / revision checks; do not generalize one family's update behavior.

entries.title: SSH hosts
entries.text: For ssh.hosts.add / update. This records where / how to connect and which key to use; hosts. stores fingerprints instead. {"id":"example-host","activeversion":"CURRENTVERSION","host":"192.0.2.20","port":22,"username":"YOURUSER","authtype":"key","keyid":"example-key","enabled":true} Field Type, limit, and meaning id Stable string, at most 31 bytes; must not already exist for add; must exist for update host Address string, at most 63 bytes port SSH integer port, normally22; use1-65535 username Remote user, at most 31 bytes; distinct from device login authtype key / password; key is recommended for persistent definitions keyid Saved local SSH private-key ID, at most 31 bytes enabled Boolean, decoding default true createdtime Optional unsigned 32-bit time value; normally retain the existing value The persistent model does not store a password field. password mode does not imply a saved remote password; immediate calls supply their own credentials. At most16 hosts. Address, key existence, and remote trust are checked separately.

entries.title: SSH commands
entries.text: For ssh.commands.add / update. Saving does not execute a command. Use servicemode:false for short commands; managed long-running services use true and ssh.services.start. {"id":"example-command","activeversion":"CURRENTVERSION","hostid":"example-host","name":"Read OS","command":"uname -a","timeoutsec":30,"enabled":true,"servicemode":false} Field Type, limit, and meaning id / hostid Strings, at most 31 bytes each; hostid references a saved host name / command Strings, at most63 /1023 bytes desc / icon Optional strings, at most127 /63 bytes; icon can be a display icon or path expectpattern / failpattern / extractpattern Optional match / extraction patterns, at most 127 bytes each varname Optional result-variable prefix, at most 31 bytes timeoutsec 0-65535 seconds, default 30; not milliseconds stoponmatch / nohup / enabled / servicemode Booleans; enabled defaults true, others false readypattern / servicefailpattern Service readiness / failure patterns, at most 127 bytes each readytimeoutsec / readycheckintervalms Integers0-65535, seconds / milliseconds respectively; configure deliberately for services createdtime Optional unsigned 32-bit time value Aliases are timeout, expectPattern, failPattern, extractPattern, varName, stopOnMatch, serviceMode, readyPattern, serviceFailPattern, readyTimeout, readyInterval. Prefer table names; avoid supplying both aliases. objectid / runtimeinstance represent persistent / runtime identity; retain returned values rather than inventing them. At most64 commands.

entries.title: Data sources
entries.text: For automation.sources.add / update. Sources acquire data and map it to variables used by rules. {"id":"example-source","activeversion":"CURRENTVERSION","label":"Temperature","type":"rest","enabled":false,"pollintervalms":5000,"autodiscover":false,"resturl":"https://example.com/status","restmethod":"GET","mappings":[{"path":"temperature","var":"compute.temperature"}]} Shared field Type and meaning id / label Strings, at most63 /47 bytes type builtin / websocket / socketio / rest / variable strings, or corresponding integers0-4 enabled / autodiscover Booleans; autodiscover defaults true; example explicitly disables it pollintervalms Integer0-4294967295 milliseconds; update behavior depends on type; zero is not unlimited sampling mappings At most4: path up to 95 bytes, var up to 63 bytes, optional transform up to 63 bytes Mapping path / var also accept jsonpath / varname. The path locates a field in data, such as temperature or cpu.cores[0].freq; it is not a URL. Verify transforms with known sample values. Type Type-specific fields websocket wsuri up to 95 bytes; wspath legacy single-field path up to 63 bytes; reconnectms0-65535 ms socketio siourl up to 95 bytes; sioevent up to 63 bytes rest resturl up to 95 bytes; restmethod up to 7 bytes; restauth up to 47 bytes; restpath legacy path up to 63 bytes variable varname, varprefix, varwatchall; SSH data flows also use sshhostid, sshcommand, expectpattern, failpattern, extractpattern, timeoutsec builtin builtin object: type selects a built-in sample; GPIO uses pin, ADC uses channel / atten, computer state can use deviceindex String-type inputs also accept convenience aliases: WebSocket uri / jsonpath; Socket.IO url / event; REST url / method / authheader / jsonpath. Prefer canonical fields above. Variable-source strings are generally at most 63 bytes, sshcommand 95 bytes, timeoutsec0-65535 seconds. For built-in numeric hardware type / channel IDs, start from existing definitions rather than guessing pins or channels.

entries.title: User variables
entries.text: automation.variables.set writes; get / list reads. Name, source, readonly, and age matter in addition to value. {"name":"example.temperature","value":42.5,"activeversion":"CURRENTVERSION"} value supports null, boolean, finite number, or a string up to 63 bytes. Normally omit valuetype for inference. Explicit types are0=null,1=bool,2=int,3=float,4=string and must match. Integers use signed 32-bit range; other finite numeric values use floating point. sourceid defaults to user. createonly:true preserves an existing variable, so it does not establish that the new requested value was written. Readonly / system-source variables can reject changes. Temperature binding requires suitable numeric temperature variables; strings, invalid values, and stale data are not normal sensor readings.

entries.title: Action templates
entries.text: automation.actions.add / update saves reusable actions. This example logs a message rather than controlling hardware. {"id":"example-action","activeversion":"CURRENTVERSION","name":"Record a message","enabled":true,"type":"log","async":false,"delayms":0,"log":{"level":3,"message":"Example action"}} Shared fields: id up to 63 bytes, name 47 bytes, description 63 bytes; enabled defaults true, async false; delayms0-65535 milliseconds. createdat is an optional nonnegative integer time value, normally retained from the existing object. type Type-specific subobject and fields log log: level, message up to 47 bytes setvar setvar: variable, value, optional valuetype sshcmd ssh: hostref, command, timeoutms, async sshcmdref sshref: cmdid referencing a saved command gpio gpio: pin, level as a boolean, pulsems devicectrl device: device, action using supported actions cli cli: command, varname, timeoutms webhook webhook: url, method, bodytemplate led led: device, ctrltype and fields for that display function Host references, variable names, command references, and device / action names are generally up to 63 bytes. Inline SSH / CLI commands and webhook URL are up to 95 bytes, method 7 bytes, bodytemplate 63 bytes. Overlong fields are rejected; do not rely on truncation. Inline action commands have less capacity than saved ssh.commands.

entries.title: LED action fields
entries.text: led.ctrltype is fill / effect / brightness / off / text / image / qrcode / filter / filterstop / textstop. Supply fields for the chosen function, not every parameter from a direct LED API. Shared display fields: device, index (255=all), color string or r / g / b, brightness0-255, effect, speed, durationms0-65535. Matrix fields: text up to 127 bytes, font31, imagepath127, qrtext255, qrecc string L / M / Q / H, filter31, filterparams, center, loop, scroll, align, x / y, autopos for text positioning. scroll is none / left / right / up / down; align left / center / right; x / y signed 16-bit coordinates. QR foreground uses qrfg; background uses qrbgimage. Explicit black is an intentional color, not an omitted value. filterparams uses named numeric options supported by the effect. Execution additionally requires supported hardware and valid paths / configuration. Save / read before deliberately testing an effect.

entries.title: Automation rules
entries.text: automation.rules.add / update saves conditions and actions. Enabled rules can begin executing automatically; initially set enabled:false. {"id":"example-rule","activeversion":"CURRENTVERSION","name":"Temperature example","enabled":false,"logic":"and","cooldownms":10000,"conditions":[{"variable":"example.temperature","operator":"gt","value":50}],"actions":[{"type":"log","level":3,"message":"Temperature high"}]} Field Type and meaning id / name / icon Strings, at most63 /47 /63 bytes; ID rejects separators / control characters enabled Boolean, default true; example explicitly disables it manualtrigger / showondashboard / allowmanualtrigger Booleans for triggering / presentation, not caller privilege cooldownms Unsigned 32-bit milliseconds revision Rule revision; use read revision as expectedrevision for update conditions logic / conditions and / or, default and; up to 255 conditions actions Up to 255 entries; enabled rule cannot have no actions A condition is {variable, operator, value}; operators eq / ne / lt / le / gt / ge / contains. Values follow the variable model. conditions:{logic, items:[...]} is also accepted; choose one representation. Inline rule actions use flat fields: log has level / message, SSH has hostref / command, GPIO has pin / level. Templates use nested subobjects instead. Inline SSH type is ssh; template type is sshcmd. A templateid reference takes precedence over cached inline fields. Shared action fields: delayms, async, repeatmode (once / whiletrue / count), repeatcount0-255, repeatintervalms0-65535, optional condition (condition model; null clears it). Select repetition with the action's effects in mind. Inline type Flat fields log / setvar level / message; or variable / value / valuetype ssh / sshcmdref hostref / command / sshasync / timeoutms; or cmdid gpio / devicectrl pin / boolean level / pulsems; or device / action webhook / cli url / method / bodytemplate; or command / varname / timeoutms led Flat device / ctrltype / r / g / b etc.; ctrltype uses an integer enum rather than template strings Prefer referencing a saved template for complex LED rules. Inline ctrltype:0 fill,1 effect,2 brightness,3 off,4 text,5 image,6 qrcode,7 filter,8 filterstop,9 textstop. Inline qrecc is a character-code integer: L76 / M77 / Q81 / H72. filterparams remains its own object. Integer ranges: speed1-100; intensity / density / decay / amplitude0-255; scale1-100; levels 2-16; amount / saturation / frequency0-100; angle0-360; width1-16; wavelength1-32. These template / UI units differ from some direct LED filter units. Do not place an entire API request into the actions array.

entries.title: Module configuration
entries.text: config.module.show returns the module's config object. Read existing fields before config.module.set changes one key. Modules: net / dhcp / wifi / nat / led / fan / device / system. See individual operations for all support. key is local to the module; preserve the value type. config.module.save and dirty state are separate from automation activeversion. Networking changes can interrupt access; record the access route first. WiFi views below ADMIN omit passwords.

entries.title: Monitoring widgets
entries.text: ui.widgets stores frontend layout JSON; it does not create collectors. widgets is a frontend-interpreted array and may initially be empty. Start from ui.widgets.get and retain existing fields / IDs. refreshinterval is milliseconds, default 5000. Whole serialized configuration is limited to 4000 bytes. nvssaved does not imply that a variable has data.

entries.title: Import, deletion, and source selection
entries.text: Use preview then apply with the preview's preconditions. tscfg is complete package JSON as a string, not an arbitrary object. Hosts, commands, sources, and actions import use expecteddigest / expectedcredential. Rule import has different confirmation fields; see its reference. Preview deletion impact before selecting ordinary deletion, replacement, or cascade. Deleting definitions does not automatically stop remote processes or revoke remote keys. SD / internal-backup selection replaces the configuration set; use automation.config.preview / apply rather than overwriting protected files.

entries.title: WebSocket integration
entries.text: Connect to ws://10.10.99.97/ws, replacing the address with your device IP. This channel provides telemetry, logs, controller commands, and interactive SSH. A successful connection alone does not authorize private functions.

entries.title: Authenticate and subscribe
entries.text: Obtain token through HTTP login, then send: {"type":"auth","token":"YOURTOKEN"} Wait for authok; failure returns autherror. Ordinary telemetry topics are currently public, but establishing authentication remains useful for protected functions. Authentication cannot elevate a READ session to ROOT. {"type":"subscribe","topic":"fan.status","params":{"interval":5000}} Successful acknowledgement: {"type":"subscribed","topic":"fan.status","success":true} Illustrative data envelope: {"type":"data","topic":"fan.status","timestamp":123,"data":{"fans":[]}} timestamp is seconds since start; HTTP measurements and logs may use milliseconds. Subscription success is not proof that the first reading has arrived. If updates stop, inspect channel / source state and use HTTP readback as needed.

entries.title: Topics
entries.text: Topic Default / minimum display interval Content system.dashboard 1000 ms cpu / memory / info / network / power / fan / services; unavailable sections may be omitted system.info 5000 ms Controller information system.memory 5000 ms Controller memory system.cpu 1000 ms Controller CPU network.status 5000 ms Network status power.status 5000 ms Power status fan.status 5000 ms Fans service.list 5000 ms Controller services device.status Event-driven, default 2000 ms Computer state events, not a periodic complete snapshot ota.progress Event-driven, default 1000 ms Device-wide progress; check HTTP progress and the version after restart config.pack.validated Event-driven, default 0 Uploaded package validation, not configuration application params.interval is a nonnegative integer in milliseconds. The first eight periodic topics reject0 and raise smaller intervals to their minimum. An interval does not convert the last three event topics into polling. Re-subscribing to the same topic on a connection updates that subscription; it does not create a history queue. Unsubscribe with {"type":"unsubscribe","topic":"fan.status"} and inspect unsubscribed / success. {"type":"ping"} receives pong. Pong does not establish session authorization or healthy telemetry.

entries.title: Logs
entries.text: ADMIN or higher is required. Authenticate, then send logsubscribe. History also requires ADMIN. Outgoing type Fields Result / effect logsubscribe minLevel, default VERBOSE logsubscribed / minLevel, then type=log logsetlevel minLevel Changes this connection's filter, not all module output levels loggethistory limit default 500; minLevel ERROR; maxLevel VERBOSE loghistory with logs / total, bounded by buffer capacity logunsubscribe None Stops this connection's log stream Log entries contain timestamp in milliseconds since start, level, levelName, tag, message, and task. Levels 0-5 are NONE / ERROR / WARN / INFO / DEBUG / VERBOSE. Retention is bounded; reconnect does not automatically replay history.

entries.title: Controller command terminal
entries.text: This terminal controls the management controller, not the Linux system on either computer. ROOT is required and commands can change hardware / configuration. Outgoing type Fields Result terminalstart token Binds and requests the terminal; connected includes prompt; occupancy returns terminalbusy / retryafter terminalinput data: complete command string output / data messages, then done with code / outputincomplete / stopped terminalinterrupt None Requests interruption; commandstopping may precede done terminalstop None Releases this connection's terminal, not a rollback of external effects Only one terminal owner is active at a time. Do not take over a live terminal. Missing output does not by itself prove execution failure. Prefer structured HTTP state APIs over parsing terminal output for a first integration.

entries.title: Interactive SSH Shell
entries.text: ROOT is required. sshconnect carries token and binds the connection. Verify remote fingerprints first; this Shell has no automatic unknown-fingerprint acceptance switch. Outgoing type Fields Result sshconnect token, host, user; optional port22 / password for this remote login sshstatus connecting / connected / error; this entry uses password authentication sshinput data Writes text; explicitly include required newlines sshresize width, height Integers1-65535 for terminal columns / rows sshsignal signal Sends a supported signal; unsupported requests fail sshdisconnect None Disconnects this connection's Shell; observe final sshstatus Output uses sshoutput / data, status uses sshstatus / status / message. A connection controls only its own Shell. Do not replay input automatically after a failed control or disconnect; the remote side may have received it.

entries.title: HTTP-started streaming SSH
entries.text: ssh.execstream starts through HTTP and returns sessionid / bootid / resultkey. It is separate from the interactive Shell. Authenticate WebSocket before starting to avoid missing early events. Private events are delivered only to connections authorized for the initiating session. Incoming type Fields and interpretation sshexecstart sessionid, command and patterns; started, not completed sshexecoutput sessionid, outputoffset, outputlength, isstderr, datab64 sshexecmatch sessionid, expectmatched / failmatched, optional extracted / isfinal sshexecrunning In-progress response from HTTP status query sshexecdone sessionid, executionstatus, exitcode, status / success and matches sshexeccancelled sessionid, executionstatus; cancellation does not establish remote process termination sshexecerror sessionid, error, optional stage / detail Decode datab64 into bytes, verify outputlength, and use outputoffset to detect gaps / duplicates. Stream UTF-8 decoding across frames; characters can span messages. Terminal results may include outputbytes / outputincomplete / collectiontruncated / conditionscomplete. Execution completion, condition matching, and output completeness are separate. exitcode=0 can coexist with missing output; incomplete matching is not a positive result. After disconnect, query ssh.execstatus with the receipt; it does not rerun the command or promise all historical output.

entries.title: Capacity and reconnection
entries.text: This build allows eight WebSocket clients and 32 topic subscriptions service-wide. Large frames, slow clients, exclusive tasks, and shutdown can reject work. Input must be protocol JSON text, at most 64 KiB; do not use fragmentation as a file-upload mechanism. JSON depth limits also apply. Reconnect with delay, reauthenticate, and restore subscriptions. Do not automatically repeat terminalinput, sshinput, or HTTP controls. Display last-update age and stale / disconnected state so old values do not appear current. The companion subscribe.js example uses a browser that can reach the device and needs no third-party libraries.

entries.title: File transfer and updates
entries.text: Ordinary files and APP / WWW images use dedicated binary routes. Bodies contain original file bytes; successful responses do not necessarily include code. These routes are separate from the 277 logical API names.

entries.title: Ordinary files
entries.text: Route Method / access Request and result /api/v1/file/download GET, READ; ADMIN for sensitive paths Absolute path in query; response is file bytes, not a directory /api/v1/file/upload POST, ADMIN Destination path in query, original bytes in body; success returns path / size / status=uploaded HTTP uploads only allow validated ordinary files under /sdcard/. Other file operations, such as storage.rename / delete, have a different path scope; they do not allow HTTP upload to /spiffs/ or /www/. Sensitive configuration and private-key reads require ADMIN. Managed automation directories, aliases, backups, and temporary files remain protected; edit them through object configuration APIs. Uploads allow at most 16 MiB with a 300-second receive budget, also limited by memory, free space, and storage state. Supply one complete nonempty file. Repeated requests do not append chunks. Upload replaces an existing destination; preserve needed content first. URL-encode paths once. Configure TSBASE and TSTOKEN before running: curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 330 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \ --data-binary @example.txt \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/file/upload?path=/sdcard/example.txt" curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 60 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ --get --data-urlencode 'path=/sdcard/example.txt' \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/file/download" -o downloaded-example.txt A .tscfg upload adds configpack.valid / reason / signature information. uploaded means saved, not trusted or applied. Preview and apply through the object-specific import; config.pack.apply does not apply generic configuration. Ordinary data packages and command-bearing rule packages have different signing-usage checks; ordinary validation does not replace rule-import validation. For filereplaceuncertain or a lost connection, inspect file metadata and download its contents before retrying.

entries.title: Prepare images
entries.text: Obtain a complete APP firmware image and matching www.bin for the hardware, partition layout, and firmware version. A WWW image is not an individual HTML file. Back up configuration, ensure stable power and a maintenance window, and prepare a recovery path. Downloads accept HTTP and HTTPS. HTTPS uses system certificate trust by default. skipverify is a download option; it cannot fix damaged or incompatible images or insufficient capacity. Normally keep it false. Current start APIs do not accept a private-CA certpem parameter.

entries.title: Choose a transfer method
entries.text: Method API Requirements Device downloads ota.starturl / ota.www.start Device can reach the image server; check network and storage SD file ota.startfile / ota.www.startsdcard Mounted SD with complete image files Client uploads Dedicated binary routes below Client has complete files; device has writable SD for staging and recovery cache Route Method / access Options and success /api/v1/ota/firmware POST, ADMIN Complete APP body; autoreboot query defaults true; status=success, size, message, rebootpending, autorebootrequested /api/v1/ota/www POST, ADMIN Complete www.bin body; status=success, size, message; no automatic restart Both allow at most 16 MiB with a 300-second receive budget, subject to target-partition capacity and memory. Firmware headers and installation completeness are checked. Successful upload saves SD recovery files and a manifest with automatic recovery disabled; application acceptance after restart remains a separate step. This example disables automatic restart so the maintenance process can inspect the result first: curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 600 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \ --data-binary @firmware.bin \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/ota/firmware?autoreboot=false" firmware.bin is a client-side filename; replace it with the complete firmware image. This request writes to the device. With autoreboot=true, restart is requested about 2 seconds after a successful response and the connection may close.

entries.title: Confirm progress and completion
entries.text: After URL or SD initiation, read ota.progress, or ota.www.progress for WWW. Progress is device-wide without a private per-login task receipt. Coordinate updates through one maintenance process to avoid concurrent starts or cancelling another update. curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/ota/progress" APP progress has state / percent / receivedsize / totalsize / message. WWW uses received / total and adds running. pendingreboot means a restart is needed; error means failure. 100 percent alone does not prove the new version is running. To cancel, POST an empty object to ota.abort or ota.www.abort, then confirm state before starting again. For binary uploads, use the HTTP response rather than assuming global progress identifies this request. HTTP409 with status=partial, error=recoverycachefailed, and flashwritten=true means Flash was written but the SD recovery cache was not fully saved. Inspect partitions and recovery files. A lost response also does not establish that no write occurred. After firmware installation, restart as planned, log in again, inspect ota.status / partitions, and verify application health. ota.validate confirms the current firmware; call it after health checks.

entries.title: Rollback and SD recovery
entries.text: Check ota.partitions.canrollback before ota.rollback. Rollback may restart immediately. Reconnect and verify version, configuration compatibility, and application state. SD recovery uses TianShanOS.bin, www.bin, and manifest.json under /sdcard/recovery/. armed controls whether recovery is enabled; force controls version comparison. Existing files do not establish enabled recovery. Follow the publisher's recovery procedure because recovery affects a later boot and persistent storage; uploading files alone does not prove success. No recovery preparation, status, or authorization API is exposed. Do not invent routes or treat ota.uploadbegin / end / abort as a complete segmented-transfer protocol. Ordinary integrations should use the binary routes above.

entries.title: Manage login state
entries.text: Keep one session per client process and reuse it for requests. Schedule renewal from expiresin; log in again after a clear authentication failure rather than on every poll. There are eight session slots shared by scripts and browsers. When slots are full, a new login may invalidate an older session for the same account. Normal sessions expire after 86400 seconds in this build. Restart, logout, password changes, and revocation require reauthentication. Treat tokens as opaque credentials, not values to parse or construct.

entries.title: Poll or subscribe
entries.text: Use HTTP for occasional reads and WebSocket for a continuously displayed dashboard. Subscribe only to required topics and unsubscribe when leaving a view. Display update intervals do not change hardware sampling or fan control periods. After a disconnect, reconnect, authenticate, and restore subscriptions. Do not automatically repeat power commands, SSH execution, or updates. Telemetry and logs missed during disconnection are not guaranteed to be replayed.

entries.title: Track one operation
entries.text: Streaming SSH uses sessionid+bootid+resultkey; the execution sessionid differs from the login sessionid. OTA uses device-wide progress without a private operation receipt. SSH result queries require the complete receipt and initiating login; cancellation may use just the execution sessionid from that same login. Do not share receipts. Restart, replacement, or limited retention can make results unavailable; inspect the remote state then. Coordinate OTA start, cancellation, and progress through one maintenance process, since global state is not an exclusive private task.

entries.title: Timeouts and retries
entries.text: Set connection and execution deadlines separately. Scans, network diagnostics, remote commands, and updates may take longer than ordinary reads. An HTTP timeout does not cancel server-side work. Retry queries with bounded concurrency and increasing delay. For an uncertain write, inspect state first; repeat only when you know it did not start and still need it. Prefer an explicit desired state over toggle.

entries.title: Configuration changes
entries.text: Read activeversion before writing and refresh after a conflict. Rules may also require expectedrevision. Do not overwrite complete objects from a filtered list response. Record application version, build date / time, and the capabilities used by your integration. Identical version strings can identify different repaired builds. After an upgrade, review method, role, field, and deprecation changes.

entries.title: Operational records
entries.text: Record time, target, operation type, business code, a brief reason, and non-secret operation identifiers. Store result credentials in controlled storage if retention is necessary. Ordinary logs should not contain Authorization, login bodies, private keys, or package secrets.

entries.title: Troubleshooting
entries.text: Record method, path, HTTP status, business code, reason, and operation receipt. Keep passwords, tokens, private keys, and full authorization headers out of support tickets.

entries.title: Cannot connect
entries.text: Use the current HTTP device address, such as http://10.10.99.97. The default port is80 and need not be written explicitly. Check the address, network reachability, and WebUI service state. A working mTLS diagnostic page on443 does not prove the business API is running. Once the public system.info request works, investigate login and the target feature.

entries.title: Authentication or permission failure
entries.text: HTTP401 usually means a missing, invalid, or expired session;403 usually means insufficient privilege. Some handlers report authorization errors as business errors within HTTP200. Log in again and inspect data.level. Admin can use ADMIN configuration and maintenance APIs; raw SSH execution, automation definition writes, and selected account management still require ROOT. Initial default passwords are rm01; use the current password if it has been changed. Password changes revoke affected sessions. Wait out login lockout instead of launching repeated concurrent retries.

entries.title: Missing temperatures or telemetry
entries.text: Inspect temp.sources for validity, update time, age, and source. Variable temperature input can be partly stale, so check valid weights / counts. monitor.data depends on a monitoring service on the compute host; inspect monitor connection and address configuration. Powered-on hardware does not guarantee telemetry has arrived.

entries.title: Accepted but unfinished
entries.text: Preserve and query the receipt or run record. SSH requires final status, exit code, and output completeness; managed services require verified state; OTA requires device-wide progress, partition state, and the running version after restart. started, cancelrequested, or a historical record alone is insufficient.

entries.title: Configuration changed
entries.text: For configurationchanged or a version conflict, reread current state and the relevant object. Compare and merge your unsaved input before submitting the new version. Do not simply replace the version token and repeat a delete / import / overwrite request.

entries.title: Save failed or outcome unknown
entries.text: Inspect applied, persisted, saved, uncertain, resultunknown, and the reason. Runtime state can change even when persistence fails. Read it back, then check saved startup configuration or backups as applicable. A network failure does not establish that the request had no effect.

entries.title: SSH fingerprint changed
entries.text: Stop automatic retries and obtain the current fingerprint from the server administrator. Check for reinstall, replacement, or address reassignment. Use the documented confirmation fields only after verification. An identical address does not guarantee the same host.

entries.title: Busy or at capacity
entries.text: Reduce concurrency, reuse sessions, and close unused subscriptions or terminals. Inspect active work. Tasks cannot queue indefinitely because a client keeps retrying. Wait for your own task's stop sequence; do not take over another connection's work.

entries.title: Upload or update failed
entries.text: Check role, complete request delivery, path, SD status, free capacity, target partition size, and complete images for the hardware / partition layout. Uploaded does not mean package validation or installation succeeded. For SSH, query the retained receipt; for OTA, inspect global progress and partition state before retrying, rolling back, or deleting recovery material.

entries.title: Version and compatibility
entries.text: This guide is based on TianshanOS 0.6.4. It remains useful for later versions where interfaces and procedures are unchanged. If parameters or results differ, follow the documentation for your installed version.

entries.title: Connections and accounts
entries.text: Item Usage Business API HTTP, default port 80, prefix /api/v1; e.g. http://10.10.99.97 Live messages WebSocket, ws://device-address / ws Default accounts admin / root, both initially rm01; use the current password if changed Session authentication Login token in Authorization: Bearer Access control Minimum role per endpoint, with additional resource / version / ownership checks

entries.title: Feature prerequisites
entries.text: An available endpoint does not establish that all runtime dependencies are ready. Inspect the relevant status before use. Feature Prerequisites Temperature, fans, power, computers Initialized drivers, existing targets, valid measurements Compute telemetry Running monitor, reachable host service, fresh valid data Files and SD updates Required storage mounted, file present, sufficient capacity; direct upload has a separate flow SSH / SFTP and managed services Network, credentials, host fingerprints, keys, saved configuration, task capacity Automation Loaded / enabled configuration, correct engine state, valid references, matching write versions Configuration packages Device / recipient identity and publisher trust; export also requires Developer capability Device PKI and updates Valid PKI material / time for diagnostics; complete compatible APP / WWW images for updates Matrix content Supported target and usable font / image files

entries.title: Aliases and unsupported entries
entries.text: config.pack.apply is retained but does not apply generic configuration; use the object-specific import. led.set writes pixel ranges. ota.uploadbegin / end / abort control an upload, but no public uploadwrite data API is provided; ordinary integrations should use complete-image binary upload. OTA retains upgradeurl / starturl and upgradefile / startfile aliases. Prefer starturl / startfile for new integrations.

entries.title: mTLS diagnostic service
entries.text: This separate certificate-authenticated service defaults to 443. It is not another port for /api/v1. Availability depends on PKI material, configuration, and service state. Bearer tokens do not replace client certificates. Method/path Minimum certificate role Purpose GET / anonymous Health GET /api/auth/whoami viewer Certificate identity GET /api/test/viewer viewer Read-role test GET /api/test/operator operator Operator-role test GET /api/test/admin admin Admin read test POST /api/test/admin-action admin Admin write test These endpoints diagnose health, identity, and permissions rather than performing device business actions. Certificate viewer / operator / admin and business READ / ADMIN / ROOT belong to separate identity systems and cannot be interchanged.

entries.title: Included examples
entries.text: The PDF includes readstatus.py and subscribe.js as attachments. Save them using a PDF reader that supports attachments; the editable companion contains the same files. Placeholder addresses, tokens, and certificate paths are not actual device settings.

entries.title: Copy a code example
entries.text: Code boxes contain selectable text without line numbers mixed into the code. To preserve indentation and line endings exactly, use the paperclip in the upper-right corner to save the named source file, or save it from your PDF reader's attachment panel. If your reader does not support attachments, the download package contains all original examples in code-examples / en with matching filenames. Save API request JSON as request.json for the corresponding endpoint. Response examples and WebSocket messages serve the purposes described in their chapters. Fill in addresses, tokens, and other placeholders before use.

entries.title: Python read-only query
entries.text: Python 3 and its standard library are sufficient. Use your device address and run: python3 readstatus.py --base 'http://10.10.99.97' \ --user admin Enter the password at the hidden prompt rather than in command history. The script logs in, reads status, and attempts logout. It does not control hardware, run remote tasks, or upgrade. It follows no redirects and performs no automatic retries. Check valid / dutyvalid and other measurement flags in its output.

entries.title: Browser subscription
entries.text: subscribe.js exports watchTianShan as an ES module without third-party libraries. Use a browser that can reach the device. Obtain a token through HTTP login first: import {watchTianShan} from './subscribe.js'; const close = watchTianShan({ baseUrl: 'http://10.10.99.97', token: yourLoginToken, onData: message => renderYourDashboard(message.data), onState: state => showConnectionState(state) }); Your page supplies renderYourDashboard / showConnectionState. Call close() when leaving. Mark readings stale after disconnect before restoring authentication / subscriptions. Keep tokens out of source, URLs, and ordinary logs. The example does not reconnect automatically or replay actions.

entries.title: Complete API index
entries.text: All 277 registered names are included. Select a name to jump to an entry. Each entry lists the allowed methods, minimum access level, parameters, and checks for completion. Send the reference request examples as POST JSON. Save an example as request.json, replace the placeholders, and call the listed path. Public calls may omit Authorization. curl --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 60 \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TSTOKEN" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @request.json \ "$TSBASE/api/v1/PATHFROMREFERENCE" Writes have real effects. Obtain the required versions, object IDs, certificates, or release materials first. Use GET only where it is explicitly allowed; use POST JSON for complex parameters.

entries.title: Alphabetical locator
entries.text: The labels indicate the minimum access level for an entry. Resource, session, and feature requirements still apply. Retained but unsupported entries are marked in the reference.

entries.title: Accounts and sessions APIs
entries.text: Complete index Common rules Troubleshooting Examples are POST JSON bodies with illustrative values. Response descriptions refer to data unless explicitly stated otherwise. API Purpose auth.admin.resetpassword Restore the admin default password auth.admin.setpassword Root sets admin password auth.changepassword Change password auth.login User login auth.logout User logout auth.root.setpassword Root sets root password auth.status Check auth status

entries.title: auth.admin.resetpassword
entries.text: Restore the admin default password Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/admin/resetpassword Minimum access: ROOT

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted token string Required Valid login token in JSON; sessionid is not a substitute. No default

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "token": "ROOTTOKEN" }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.success / username / passwordchanged. After success, admin logs in with default password rm01.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Root restores the admin password to rm01. Use that default password after reset.

entries.title: auth.admin.setpassword
entries.text: Root sets admin password Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/admin/setpassword Minimum access: ROOT

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted token string Required Valid login token in JSON; sessionid is not a substitute. No default newpassword string Required New password, 4-64 bytes. No default

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "token": "ROOTTOKEN", "newpassword": "NEWPASSWORD" }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.success / sessionsrevoked / reauthrequired / username / passwordchanged. Affected-account sessions are revoked.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Both the Authorization identity and the JSON token must pass root checks; both fields have a purpose.

entries.title: auth.changepassword
entries.text: Change password Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/changepassword Minimum access: Body token (authentication-specific)

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted token string Required Valid login token in JSON; sessionid is not a substitute. No default oldpassword string Required Current password. No default newpassword string Required New password, 4-64 bytes. No default

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "token": "YOURTOKEN", "oldpassword": "CURRENTPASSWORD", "newpassword": "NEWPASSWORD" }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.success / sessionsrevoked / reauthrequired. Log in again after success.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: The account holder chooses when to change the password. The old session is invalidated after success.

entries.title: auth.login
entries.text: User login Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/login Minimum access: Public

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted username string Required Configured admin or root account. No default password string Required Current password for that account. No default

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "username": "admin", "password": "rm01" }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: POST success has code=0 and data.token / sessionid / username / level / expiresin(seconds)/passwordchanged.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Five consecutive failures lock login for 300 seconds. Login does not establish WebSocket subscriptions.

entries.title: auth.logout
entries.text: User logout Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/logout Minimum access: Body token (authentication-specific)

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: No business parameters.

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: Dedicated POST returns {success:true}. Also discard the client token.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Authorization identifies the session to close; no JSON is needed. The internal handler's body-token form is not the dedicated HTTP POST contract.

entries.title: auth.root.setpassword
entries.text: Root sets root password Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/root/setpassword Minimum access: ROOT

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted token string Required Valid login token in JSON; sessionid is not a substitute. No default newpassword string Required New password, 4-64 bytes. No default

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "token": "ROOTTOKEN", "newpassword": "NEWPASSWORD" }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.success / sessionsrevoked / reauthrequired / username / passwordchanged. Affected-account sessions are revoked.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Both the Authorization identity and the JSON token must pass root checks; both fields have a purpose.

entries.title: auth.status
entries.text: Check auth status Methods: POST Path: /api/v1/auth/status Minimum access: Body token (authentication-specific)

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted token string Required Valid login token in JSON; sessionid is not a substitute. No default

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "token": "YOURTOKEN" }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.valid reports validity; valid sessions include username / level / expiresin / passwordchanged. valid=false can coexist with code=0.

API Purpose system.apis List all registered APIs system.cpu Get CPU core statistics system.info Get system information system.log.level Get / set log level system.memory Get memory information system.memorydetail Get detailed memory analysis system.reboot Reboot the system system.tasks Get task list

entries.text: { "level": 3 }

entries.title: Usage notes

entries.text: Get detailed memory analysis Methods: GET / POST Path: /api/v1/system/memorydetail Minimum access: ADMIN

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Estimates in one diagnostic snapshot are not an exact physical-memory breakdown or proof of a leak.

entries.text: data.status=rebooting, delayms, and waitingformaintenance=false. Restart is requested after the delay; this API does not wait for an update to finish.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Interrupts management connectivity. Save required settings, wait for recovery, and log in again.

entries.title: Fans APIs

entries.title: fan.config
entries.text: Get fan configuration including curve Methods: GET / POST Path: /api/v1/fan/config Minimum access: READ

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted id integer Optional Fan ID; obtain it from fan.status first. All when omitted

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: One / all configurations: id / mode / minduty / maxduty / invertpwm / hysteresis / mininterval / curve. Curve points use temp(Celsius)/duty(percent).

entries.title: fan.curve
entries.text: Set temperature curve for fan Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/fan/curve Minimum access: ADMIN

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted id integer Required Fan ID within the device's supported range. No default curve array Required At most 10 {temp:Celsius,duty:percent} points; ascending temperatures and duty 0-100. No default hysteresis number Optional Temperature hysteresis, 0-20 Celsius. Current value mininterval integer Optional Minimum adjustment interval, integer 100-60000 milliseconds. Current value

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "id": 0, "curve": [ { "temp": 30, "duty": 30 }, { "temp": 60, "duty": 80 } ], "hysteresis": 3, "mininterval": 2000 }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.id / points / applied / persisted.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Curve configuration and control mode are separate. Read back configuration and select curve mode if needed.

entries.title: fan.enable
entries.text: Enable or disable a fan Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/fan/enable Minimum access: ADMIN

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted id integer Required Fan ID within the device's supported range. No default enable boolean Required true enables; false disables. No default

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "id": 0, "enable": true }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.id / enabled.

entries.title: Usage notes
entries.text: Disabling can reduce cooling. Check temperature and protection separately.

entries.title: fan.limits
entries.text: Set duty cycle limits (min / max) Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/fan/limits Minimum access: ADMIN

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted id integer Required Fan ID within the device's supported range. No default minduty integer Optional Minimum duty, 0-100 percent, no greater than maximum. Current value maxduty integer Optional Maximum duty, 0-100 percent. Current value

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "id": 0, "minduty": 20, "maxduty": 100 }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.id / minduty / maxduty / applied / persisted.

entries.title: fan.mode

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted id integer Required Fan ID within the device's supported range. No default mode string Required off / manual / auto / curve. No default

entries.title: Request example
entries.text: { "id": 0, "mode": "auto" }

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.id / mode / applied / persisted. Distinguish runtime application from storage failure.

entries.title: fan.save
entries.text: Save fan configuration to NVS Methods: POST / PUT / DELETE Path: /api/v1/fan/save Minimum access: ADMIN

entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: Field Type Requirement Meaning If omitted id integer Optional Fan ID. All fans

entries.title: Response and completion
entries.text: data.status / persisted. Inspect failure details; do not assume retention after restart.

entries.title: fan.set
